We are looking for a technical AI product leader to join the AI & Innovation team in the Global Private Bank. This is a hands-on builder and product leader: you will design and build AI prototypes, determine which ideas are worth scaling, and own the product outcome through the Labs-to-Products transition and beyond. Working at the intersection of AI engineering, data science, and product management, you will partner with advisors, product teams, and technology and control partners to turn emerging AI capabilities into solutions that create measurable value for clients and the firm. This role combines hands-on building with end-to-end ownership of product outcomes.

Design, code, and build AI prototypes hands-on from end to end, spanning data and technical architecture, agentic workflows, orchestration, evaluation, and working demonstrations

Experience designing evaluations and using evidence to assess technical performance, risk, user experience, and potential business value

Experience in private banking, wealth management, financial services, or another regulated environment
Experience moving AI prototypes into production in partnership with engineering, product, architecture, and control teams

title.value: Data & AI Product Manager Vice President

description.value:
Job Description

Build trusted enterprise data products that power analytics, artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) and large language model (LLM)-enabled experiences at scale. This is not a traditional backlog-management role. You will move from an ambiguous business question to hands-on data discovery, sound data and metric design, and a production capability that creates measurable business value.

As an Vice President, Data and AI Product in the Chief Data Office, you will lead the discovery, design, and delivery of trusted enterprise data products that create measurable business value at scale. You will work at the intersection of business strategy, data science, analytics, and data engineering to define reusable datasets, metrics, and analytical capabilities. You will stay accountable from initial discovery through adoption and measurable business impact.
You will work with large, complex datasets across multiple systems and domains, determine how data should be modeled and connected, and create trusted data products that power analytics, dashboards, AI/ML, and LLM-enabled experiences across the organization. You will join a team building new enterprise data capabilities, with the opportunity to solve difficult data problems at significant scale.
Job responsibilities
• Start with the business problem and work with senior business leaders and users to understand the decisions they are trying to make, identify where data or AI can materially improve those decisions, and define the data products required to make that possible.
• Explore large and often complex legacy data environments using SQL and modern data platforms to understand available data, relationships, gaps, history, and quality before determining the product solution.
• Design useful data products with data engineers, architects, and data scientists to determine how data from multiple domains should be modeled, joined, and curated to create reusable datasets, metrics, and analytical capabilities.
• Create trusted metrics by translating business concepts into precise definitions, determining the underlying data logic and joins, reconciling conflicting definitions, and establishing reusable SQL and metric logic that produces consistent results across products.
• Improve metadata, lineage, business definitions, and catalog content so analysts, data scientists, applications, and AI agents can reliably discover and interpret data.
• Partner with data science and AI/ML teams to understand analytical and model requirements, identify the right underlying data and features, and translate business questions into scalable analytical and AI-enabled products.
• Shape curated data and semantic foundations that support dashboards and traditional analytics as well as LLM, agent-based (agentic), and natural-language-to-data experiences.
• Simplify complexity by finding patterns across fragmented datasets and business processes and creating reusable data products rather than solving the same problem repeatedly for individual use cases.
• Define how success will be measured and stay accountable from initial discovery through adoption and measurable business impact.
• Challenge assumptions using data, structured thinking, and experimentation to determine the right answer rather than simply executing the solution initially requested.
Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
• 8 years of end-to-end product management experience, including substantial ownership of data-intensive products from problem discovery through production and adoption.
• Demonstrated experience creating net-new data products or analytical capabilities (not solely managing existing products, migrations, modernization, reporting programs, proofs of concept, automation, or incremental enhancements).
• Deep experience working with complex enterprise or business-to-business (B2B) data spanning multiple systems, datasets, and business domains.
• Strong, hands-on SQL capability, including independently exploring unfamiliar datasets, testing hypotheses, evaluating joins, validating data, and determining whether the data supports a proposed business metric.
• Strong understanding of data modeling, relational data, dimensional concepts, semantic and metrics layers, and analytical data products.
• Experience partnering closely with data scientists, AI/ML teams, analytics teams, and data engineers to turn ambiguous business problems into production data and analytical capabilities.
• Experience with modern enterprise data platforms and ecosystems such as Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, dbt, Spark, or comparable technologies.
• Experience building products consumed through business intelligence (BI) and analytics platforms such as Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or comparable technologies.
• Demonstrated ability to move fluidly from executive-level business discussions to detailed data investigation.
• Exceptional problem-solving and conceptual-thinking ability, including breaking down ambiguous problems systematically, investigating evidence, and developing solutions others may not have initially considered.
• Track record of influencing across a complex, highly matrixed organization and making sound product decisions when the answer is not obvious.
Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills
• Working knowledge of LLMs, generative AI, and/or agentic analytics, including how structured enterprise data, metadata, semantic definitions, and trusted metrics enable effective AI experiences.

Job Description
Build trusted enterprise data products that power analytics, artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) and large language model (LLM)-enabled experiences at scale. This is not a traditional backlog-management role. You will move from an ambiguous business question to hands-on data discovery, sound data and metric design, and a production capability that creates measurable business value.
As an Vice President, Data and AI Product in the Chief Data Office, you will lead the discovery, design, and delivery of trusted enterprise data products that create measurable business value at scale. You will work at the intersection of business strategy, data science, analytics, and data engineering to define reusable datasets, metrics, and analytical capabilities. You will stay accountable from initial discovery through adoption and measurable business impact.
You will work with large, complex datasets across multiple systems and domains, determine how data should be modeled and connected, and create trusted data products that power analytics, dashboards, AI/ML, and LLM-enabled experiences across the organization. You will join a team building new enterprise data capabilities, with the opportunity to solve difficult data problems at significant scale.
Job responsibilities
• Start with the business problem and work with senior business leaders and users to understand the decisions they are trying to make, identify where data or AI can materially improve those decisions, and define the data products required to make that possible.
• Explore large and often complex legacy data environments using SQL and modern data platforms to understand available data, relationships, gaps, history, and quality before determining the product solution.
• Design useful data products with data engineers, architects, and data scientists to determine how data from multiple domains should be modeled, joined, and curated to create reusable datasets, metrics, and analytical capabilities.
• Create trusted metrics by translating business concepts into precise definitions, determining the underlying data logic and joins, reconciling conflicting definitions, and establishing reusable SQL and metric logic that produces consistent results across products.
• Improve metadata, lineage, business definitions, and catalog content so analysts, data scientists, applications, and AI agents can reliably discover and interpret data.
• Partner with data science and AI/ML teams to understand analytical and model requirements, identify the right underlying data and features, and translate business questions into scalable analytical and AI-enabled products.
• Shape curated data and semantic foundations that support dashboards and traditional analytics as well as LLM, agent-based (agentic), and natural-language-to-data experiences.
• Simplify complexity by finding patterns across fragmented datasets and business processes and creating reusable data products rather than solving the same problem repeatedly for individual use cases.
• Define how success will be measured and stay accountable from initial discovery through adoption and measurable business impact.
• Challenge assumptions using data, structured thinking, and experimentation to determine the right answer rather than simply executing the solution initially requested.
Required qualifications, capabilities, and skills
• 8 years of end-to-end product management experience, including substantial ownership of data-intensive products from problem discovery through production and adoption.
• Demonstrated experience creating net-new data products or analytical capabilities (not solely managing existing products, migrations, modernization, reporting programs, proofs of concept, automation, or incremental enhancements).
• Deep experience working with complex enterprise or business-to-business (B2B) data spanning multiple systems, datasets, and business domains.
• Strong, hands-on SQL capability, including independently exploring unfamiliar datasets, testing hypotheses, evaluating joins, validating data, and determining whether the data supports a proposed business metric.
• Strong understanding of data modeling, relational data, dimensional concepts, semantic and metrics layers, and analytical data products.
• Experience partnering closely with data scientists, AI/ML teams, analytics teams, and data engineers to turn ambiguous business problems into production data and analytical capabilities.
• Experience with modern enterprise data platforms and ecosystems such as Databricks, Snowflake, BigQuery, Redshift, dbt, Spark, or comparable technologies.
• Experience building products consumed through business intelligence (BI) and analytics platforms such as Tableau, Power BI, Looker, or comparable technologies.
• Demonstrated ability to move fluidly from executive-level business discussions to detailed data investigation.
• Exceptional problem-solving and conceptual-thinking ability, including breaking down ambiguous problems systematically, investigating evidence, and developing solutions others may not have initially considered.
• Track record of influencing across a complex, highly matrixed organization and making sound product decisions when the answer is not obvious.
Preferred qualifications, capabilities, and skills
• Working knowledge of LLMs, generative AI, and/or agentic analytics, including how structured enterprise data, metadata, semantic definitions, and trusted metrics enable effective AI experiences.

Job Description
Build trusted enterprise data products that power analytics, artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) and large language model (LLM)-enabled experiences at scale. This is not a traditional backlog-management role. You will move from an ambiguous business question to hands-on data discovery, sound data and metric design, and a production capability that creates measurable business value.
As an Vice President, Data and AI Product in the Chief Data Office, you will lead the discovery, design, and delivery of trusted enterprise data products that create measurable business value at scale. You will work at the intersection of business strategy, data science, analytics, and data engineering to define reusable datasets, metrics, and analytical capabilities. You will stay accountable from initial discovery through adoption and measurable business impact.
You will work with large, complex datasets across multiple systems and domains, determine how data should be modeled and connected, and create trusted data products that power analytics, dashboards, AI/ML, and LLM-enabled experiences across the organization. You will join a team building new enterprise data capabilities, with the opportunity to solve difficult data problems at significant scale.
Job responsibilities
• Start with the business problem and work with senior business leaders and users to understand the decisions they are trying to make, identify where data or AI can materially improve those decisions, and define the data products required to make that possible.
• Explore large and often complex legacy data environments using SQL and modern data platforms to understand available data, relationships, gaps, history, and quality before determining the product solution.
• Design useful data products with data engineers, architects, and data scientists to determine how data from multiple domains should be modeled, joined, and curated to create reusable datasets, metrics, and analytical capabilities.
• Create trusted metrics by translating business concepts into precise definitions, determining the underlying data logic and joins, reconciling conflicting definitions, and establishing reusable SQL and metric logic that produces consistent results across products.
• Improve metadata, lineage, business definitions, and catalog content so analysts, data scientists, applications, and AI agents can reliably discover and interpret data.
• Partner with data science and AI/ML teams to understand analytical and model requirements, identify the right underlying data and features, and translate business questions into scalable analytical and AI-enabled products.
• Shape curated data and semantic foundations that support dashboards and traditional analytics as well as LLM, agent-based (agentic), and natural-language-to-data experiences.
• Simplify complexity by finding patterns across fragmented datasets and business processes and creating reusable data products rather than solving the same problem repeatedly for individual use cases.
• Define how success will be measured and stay accountable from initial discovery through adoption and measurable business impact.
• Challenge assumptions using data, structured thinking, and experimentation to determine the right answer rather than simply executing the solution initially requested.

• Strong understanding of data modeling, relational data, dimensional concepts, semantic and metrics layers, and analytical data products.

• Working knowledge of LLMs, generative AI, and/or agentic analytics, including how structured enterprise data, metadata, semantic definitions, and trusted metrics enable effective AI experiences.

Joining Swayable means being on a team whose work changes the course of history. The technology we develop is at the leading edge of transforming some of the world’s most important campaign organizations and enterprises: combatting disinformation, protecting democracy, and supporting the sustainable growth of consumer-facing brands.

**About the Role**You’ll own a portfolio of product bets—new capabilities we’re investing in to expand what the Swayable platform does and deepen its value to clients—along with a set of features on our core content-testing product. You’ll bring a general manager’s mindset: you’re accountable not just for shipping, but for adoption, usage, growth, and go-to-market success—taking each bet from prototype to research preview to beta, and making clear, evidence-based go/no-go calls along the way.

Great product starts with deep client understanding and rigorous user research. You’ll earn the kind of trust where clients invite you to shadow their teams, and you’ll recruit and research users beyond our existing clients to find the problems worth solving. From there, you’ll build and test prototypes quickly—starting with what works, putting it in front of real users, measuring, and iterating.

You’ll lead how we build: partnering with engineering to shape Swayable’s AI software factory—the agents, evaluation harnesses, workflows, and tooling behind our AI software development lifecycle—so the whole team ships faster without sacrificing architectural integrity.

You’ll also bring ideas from the broader AI community—identifying groundbreaking techniques, sharing them internally, and keeping Swayable at the cutting edge of applied AI.

**What You'll Do**

* Own a portfolio of product bets plus features on the core product. Prioritize them against the company’s business objectives, and own outcomes, not just delivery.
* Take each bet through prototype, research preview, and beta: validate the problem, size the prize, build a minimum lovable product, test willingness to pay, and make a clear go/no-go call at each gate.
* Build trust-based relationships with clients deep enough to shadow their teams, understand their workflows firsthand, and identify problems they haven’t yet articulated.
* Recruit users beyond our client base and run your own research—interviews, contextual inquiry, usability tests—to understand their problems with the same depth.
* Rapidly prototype, test ideas empirically with real users, start with what works, and iterate based on evidence.
* Design, build, and evaluate complex agents—multi-step reasoning, tool use, orchestration—and integrate them into intelligent, intuitive user experiences. Define evals and quality bars, and drive continuous improvement in output quality.
* Lead the AI software development lifecycle with engineering, including building Swayable’s AI software factory: the agents, evals, and tooling that accelerate how we build every product.
* Use data and analytics to inform decision-making and iterate quickly.
* Partner with sales and customer success to drive go-to-market —validation, positioning, pricing and packaging, launch, onboarding, and adoption.
* Collaborate tightly with engineering, design, data science, and customer success—prioritizing action over process.
* Engage with the AI community to stay up to date on the latest advancements, and share knowledge with the organization.

**Who You Are**

* 5+ years of relevant professional experience and a Bachelor’s degree in a related field.
* Clear, effective communication, both written and verbal.
* Track record of building trusted relationships with clients or users—ideally to the point of being invited to shadow their work—and turning that context into products they adopt.
* Evidence of recruiting users and running research yourself, and using it to find problems worth solving.
* Evidence of rapid, empirical iteration: prototypes put in front of users, measured, and improved or killed quickly.
* Blend of analytical and design thinking—you use data to understand problems and judge what’s working, and apply design thinking principles to reframe problems, ideate collaboratively, and shape creative solutions.

ABOUT FUTURE WORKS

Large companies spend billions on consulting and implementation projects to adopt new technology. Most of that work is slow and expensive, and too often it fails to deliver. Future Works replaces it. We rebuild the operations that move a company's P&L in twelve-week cycles, run by senior experts and fleets of AI agents, with our fees tied to outcomes our clients' own finance teams verify. We deliver in twelve weeks what incumbents quote at two years.

We work with large companies in energy, construction, real estate and other asset-heavy industries. Every role here is built around humans and agents working as one system. Whatever the seat, we look for high energy, high agency and a real interest in building with AI.

THE ROLE

Our clients own real estate, and the numbers that describe it live in a dozen systems that were never designed to agree with each other. We build them a platform that fixes that, inside their own cloud, in one cycle, for a fee that does not move. As the Senior AI Product Manager, you run that cycle.

You own the plan, the gates and the scope line. You decide what the first cycle can honestly deliver, you get the client to sign up to what each gate has to prove, and you are the person the client's sponsor calls. An Operating Director owns the account. A solution architect, a data and technology lead and engineers from our shared team build it.

This is a real estate seat. You need to have done this work in the sector, because the judgment calls in this job are the ones that only make sense once you have lived through a reporting cycle.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

- Own the Cycle: Lead the engagement end to end, from discovery through build, training and handover, including retiring whatever our platform replaces.

- Hold the Scope Line: Agree with the client up front what each gate has to prove, then manage change so the fee stays fixed and what will not fit is written down rather than argued about later.

- Data Before Views: Insist the numbers are right before anything is built on top of them, and own the calls on mapping, checks and what happens when something does not reconcile.

- Where AI Belongs: Decide what the agents do and what stays on a fixed calculation, so nothing probabilistic ever lands on a number the client reports.

- Own the Client at Working Level: Be the daily contact for the sponsor and the business owner, run the workshops where the people who use the platform tell you what they need, report plainly and raise bad news early.

WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

Required Skills and Experience

- Real Estate, Hands On: At least 2 years inside or directly serving institutional owners, operators, REITs, real estate private equity or fund managers, or a real estate technology or data vendor. You can pick up a client's reporting pack and tell us what is wrong with it. Expect to be asked to do exactly that.

- Product Management: 5+ years owning every phase of the lifecycle, delivering custom software for external clients rather than an internal roadmap.

- Data Product Experience: You have shipped a reporting, BI or data platform where adoption depended on people trusting the numbers, not on the feature list.

- Fixed-Scope Delivery: You have run engagements where payment depended on the client accepting the work, and you wrote the acceptance criteria yourself.

- AI Judgment: You understand extraction, retrieval with sources, agent workflows and approval steps well enough to specify them for engineers, and you know where to keep a model out.

- Client Environment: Comfortable delivering into a client's Microsoft cloud, including access by role and by fund, audit logging and test environments.

- Leadership and Presence: You have led designers, engineers and data people, and you can tell a CFO something they do not want to hear in week three rather than week twelve.

- Analytical: You define the measures, interrogate a number you are given, and decide from evidence.

- AI-Native Workflow: You use agents in your own daily work.

- Working Hours: Overlap with US Eastern business hours.

Nice to Have

- You have switched off a system a client still depended on, including running both until they signed that the old one could go.

- Experience of the quarterly cycle that produces investor statements, or of answering investor due diligence questionnaires.

- Data governance where the business, not IT, approved the mappings and the thresholds.

OUR CULTURE & BENEFITS

We believe that breakthrough results are driven by breakthrough experiences. Our culture is built on freedom, high performance and our core values. You can read more about our values and how we work on our careers page: https://future.works/careers

Benefits & Perks

- Remote, in US Eastern hours. We work in our clients' time zones.

- Compensation. A competitive rate plus a cycle bonus.
